Overview[]

Pets are a feature added to Grow a Garden on Update 1.04.0 (May 3, 2025).

Pets possess unique abilities, having multiple of the same pets can stack their abilities. Players start with 3 equip slots, but can get an additional 5 slots from buying gamepasses from the Limited Time Shop and/or trading aged pets in.

Players can hold a maximum of 60 pets in their inventory. As of the Christmas Harvest Update, players can increase it by buying game passes in the Limited Time Shop, trading pets in, Crafting a Pet Pouch, or buying space from the Garden Ascension Shop, with a maximum of 285 pets total.

Players can craft a Pet Pouch, which adds +1 space to pet inventory. (maximum of 50 extra slots). It can be crafted with a Common Egg, a Corndog, a Small Treat, a Small Toy, and 50M Sheckles.

Garden Ascension makes it possible to increase the pet inventory again through buying pet capacity upgrade worth 40 Garden Coins per stock, which add +10 space and can be bought 15 times before becoming out of stock (including the + upgrades, which cost the same). This means players can get 150 Inventory slots from the shop.

(60 by default maximum + 25 by buying game passes or trading pets in + 50 from pet pouches + 150 from buying pet capacity upgrades from ascension shop = 285 total maximum of pet inventory)

This limit can be bypassed by getting pets from chests/rewards not buying crates. Keep in mind that to hatch an egg, the player must put it in their garden.

Pet Stats depend on their weight. As a pet grows older, its weight increases, making its abilities more efficient — such as reducing cooldowns and/or increasing passives. Mega Pets have better stats even at level 1, except for certain pets like the Triceratops, which have constant stats (regardless of base weight). In the Prehistoric Event, a pet named the Brontosaurus released, allowing players to gain increased weight upon egg hatching. Players can also increase pet age after hatching by using the Ostrich. Additionally, the Barn Owl allows players to increased store bought pets weight. The Mummy also allows players to increase the weight of pets that are obtained from chests, as long as the player has a sarcophagus placed. The Pack Mule also allows players to increase the weight of pets that are crafted

Pets can be mutated by using the Mutation Machine, a Golden Acorn, Pet Mutation Shards, or from pets like the Headless Horseman.

Age[]

Age is a pet feature which increases over time through XP (in order for the pet to increase in Age, the player must keep the hunger above 0%).

As a pet ages, the XP needed for it to level up will increase, but its traits will also improve, such as by reducing ability cooldowns., better chances, and other various buffs. A pet cannot age if its hunger bar reaches 0 (except for pets like starfish, whose passive is to gain XP).

The player can view their pet's age by clicking on the pet and choosing the "view" option, picking it up and stomping on it through their inventory, or pressing the << button on the right side of their screen and viewing the pet menu.

Traits[]

Each pet has a unique trait, which is a pet feature which can benefit the player and the player's crops. Traits like digging up seeds, increasing crop size, granting mutations to a crop, and much more are all examples of traits. The player can view the trait of a pet by clicking it and choosing the "view" option, where a description can be seen about the pet's trait.

Hunger & Feeding[]

Pets can be fed with harvested crops and food.

Hunger is a pet feature which is required in order for the pet to grow older. When the hunger bar reaches 0, the pet can no longer grow. To feed a pet, simply equip any crop from the player's inventory and move closer to the player's pet. The player can either click the pet and press the "Feed" option, or hold the interact button that appears once the player gets closer. The player can also feed their pet through the pet menu, by equipping the desired crop to be fed and selecting feed. Once a pet has been fed, a short message will appear showing a percentage by how much hunger has been restored from the player's pet. The mutation and type of fruit depends on how much a pet's hunger has been restored. Each pet can have different hunger bars, which can depend on their rarity. The player can view's the player's pet's hunger by clicking on the pet and choosing the view option, hovering the cursor over the player's pet, or by opening the pet menu by clicking the 2 white arrows on the right side of the screen.

Pets Weights[]

Pet Weight is a core feature that increases over time with age. For most pets, weights determine how strong their abilities are expressed such as reduced cooldowns or increased success rates. There are a few exceptions to this such as Triceratops and Imp which have constant stats. Additionally, many pets reach a limit where although the weight continues to increase, but their ability no longer improves, such as the Ostrich.

When hatching an egg, the weight of a pet is randomly determined. This randomized initial weight of pets not only determine the pet stats at age 1, but also the amount of weight a pet gains as it ages. Every time a pet ages it will gain an 11th of its starting weight. This means a pet at age 100 will be 10× the weight it was at age 1.

Pet weight from hatched eggs is generally 0.88-2.20kg, and pets from shops, chests, etc. range from 0.88-1.32kg. There is a 0.1% chance a pet receives the "huge" modifier, which applies an x4 multiplier to its hatch weight. Hatch weight for "huge" pets ranges from 3.52-8.80kg. The Brontosaurus can add up to 30% to the hatch weight, resulting in a max normal hatch weight of 1.14-2.86, and "huge" range of 4.56-11.44. The maximum possible hatch weight of a pet, given maximum base weight, 4x huge modifier, and 30% from Brontos, is 11.44. This makes the maximum possible weight for an Age 100 pet 114.40kg. It is not possible for a pet to exceed that weight.

The weight of a given pet at any age can be estimated through the following equation:

W 2 = W 1 A 1 + 10 ( A 2 + 10 ) {\displaystyle W_{2}={\frac {W_{1}}{A_{1}+10}}(A_{2}+10)} Where W1​ is the current weight, A1​ is the current age, A2​ is the new age, and W2 is the estimated new weight.

The age a given pet will reach a certain weight can be estimated through the following equation:

A 2 = ⌈ W 2 W 1 ( A 1 + 10 ) − 10 ⌉ {\displaystyle A_{2}=\lceil {\frac {W_{2}}{W_{1}}}({A_{1}+10})-10\rceil } Where W1​ is the current weight, A1​ is the current age, W2​ is the target weight, and A2 is the estimated age it reaches that weight.

The weight of a pet when it hatches can be estimated through the following formula (multiply the answer by 10 to get its weight on maxed age):

W b a s e = 11 ⋅ W c u r r e n t 10 + A c u r r e n t {\displaystyle W_{base}={\frac {11\cdot W_{current}}{10+A_{current}}}} Where Wbase is the weight when it hatches, the Wcurrent is the current weight, and Acurrent is the current age.

Due to lack of high accuracy data, the equation yield a 2% error which can be translated as 1kg off on a 50kg pet

Pets Loadouts Swap[]

Pets Loadout Swap was added in Update 1.18.0. This feature allows players to save and quickly swap between up to 6 custom pet loadouts.

Each loadout shares the same pet equip limit as the player's unlocked slots (see Trade in Pets for extra Pet Equip slots). Swapping between loadouts has a cooldown of 5 seconds before another swap can be made.

When swapping, all pets in the current loadout are returned to the inventory, and the pets saved in the selected loadout will be equipped one by one from the inventory.

Trivia[]

  • The Pet Menu added in Update 1.07.0 allows players to easily feed and pick up their pets by clicking 2 white arrows (<<) on the right side of the screen without having to chase their pets. It also allows players to check their pets age and XP.
  • The first pet added was the Panda. This was obtainable one hour before Update 1.04.0, where it could be seen next to the gear shop and newly added pet shop.
  • Pets can have a 1/1000 chance to become huge after hatch (3+ kg upon hatch without the use of brontosauruses.)
  • All pets are covered in classic studs (2017), except the Cooked Owl, which is weld stud texture.
  • From the 2nd of July, 2025, at approximately 4:00 am UTC, to the 9th of July, 2025, at 2:00 am UTC, pet gifting was disabled due to an exploit allowing users to duplicate pets. It has now been re-enabled.
    • Although now on July 24th 2025 it has been disabled again due to the same reasons.
  • There was a bug where if a player views the description of a pet meanwhile the person who owns the pet disconnects, they will see the description of a pet named Doge.
  • All of the unobtainable pets are still technically obtainable through gifting and storing old eggs.
  • During the Cooking Event, the Chris P's Kitchen reward "Pancake Stack Cosmetic" is particularly effective for area-effect pets such as Moon Cat, Toucan, and Blood Hedgehog, especially when focusing on cultivating a specific type of crop.
  • Apparently, In the Garden Guide, Naturally Grown Rainbow Pets are considered to be a different pet than its non-rainbow counterpart. Players can see this in the Garden Guide by checking if there are over 3 Prismatic Pets (Which both are currently are Corrupted Kitsune, Headless Horseman, and Kitsune).
  • Before pets was officially added the community Got to decide whether Pets would have no studded texture or fully studded - Studded won and all pets and future pets in-game will have a studded texture. (Certain Pet mutations may override the studded texture)
  • When checking an Uncommon Pet’s tab, the Uncommon rarity’s color is tan instead of green.
  • GIANT hatched pets were the rainbow hatch equivalent of the Premium Fall Egg.
